The Vitali Set

Pick one representative from each equivalence class using the axiom of choice. The result is a set whose size cannot be measured.

Shifted copies of this set cover a whole interval. If its size were zero, the copies would total zero. If positive, the copies would total infinity. Both contradict, so no size exists.

For example, copies of one 📦 box can fill a room, yet if the box's size were zero the total should be zero, and if it were anything more the total would explode. So the size cannot be assigned.

Show proof

  1. [Use of AC — the only one] x∼y  ⟺  x−y∈Qx \sim y \iff x - y \in \mathbb{Q}x∼y⟺x−y∈Q is an equivalence relation on [0,1][0, 1][0,1] (reflexive, symmetric, transitive because Q\mathbb{Q}Q is an additive group).

    Invoke the axiom of choice exactly once to pick one representative from each class meeting [0,1][0, 1][0,1].

    The collection of picks is VVV — so V⊂[0,1]V \subset [0, 1]V⊂[0,1] and VVV holds exactly one element from each class.

  2. Let x∈(V+q1)∩(V+q2)x \in (V + q_1) \cap (V + q_2)x∈(V+q1​)∩(V+q2​); then x=v1+q1=v2+q2x = v_1 + q_1 = v_2 + q_2x=v1​+q1​=v2​+q2​ for some v1,v2∈Vv_1, v_2 \in Vv1​,v2​∈V. Rearranging, v1−v2=q2−q1∈Qv_1 - v_2 = q_2 - q_1 \in \mathbb{Q}v1​−v2​=q2​−q1​∈Q — i.e. v1∼v2v_1 \sim v_2v1​∼v2​.

  3. Since VVV holds only one element per class, v1∼v2v_1 \sim v_2v1​∼v2​ forces v1=v2v_1 = v_2v1​=v2​.

    Then q1=x−v1=x−v2=q2q_1 = x - v_1 = x - v_2 = q_2q1​=x−v1​=x−v2​=q2​ — contradiction.

    Hence translates by distinct rationals are disjoint.
